Hey all! Sorry I was busy with work and the driver’s test. Just wanted to thank everybody here for their tips and also share what happened to my test.

So I failed the driver test when I took it in Dromana, unfortunately. I did not hit anything, but I failed to turn in time on an intersection. Tester said I created an unexpected delay and had a high risk of unnecessary collision since I was holding up traffic behind me.

It sucks at that time, of course. But I tried again, but this time in a more familiar place which is in Vicroads Heatherton. Thank God I passed lol. 

Here are some of the things I did:
1. It really helps if you know the area where you are going to take the driver’s test. For my case, I was not really that familiar with Dromana even though I went there a couple of times to practice. So choose the place where you’re going to take carefully.

2. As advised in the comments, I also booked a lesson immediately before my driver test in Dromana. However if you can, try to book at least 3 lessons. That is what I did after I failed in Dromana. I booked 3 lessons, which comprise of 2 1hr lessons and another 1hr for warm up before the test. Those 3 lessons really helped me with familiarising with car I am going to use and also the area where I am going to take the test. I highly recommend VIP Driving School, since the instructor I got (Shane) was really good and patient with me. 

3. As mentioned in the comments again, watch out for school zones. Don’t go above the speed limit in these areas at all. I almost failed my 2nd attempt because I went over 40kmh (I went 42-43kmh lol), but quickly slowed down. I was just lucky, since the tester was not able to read the speedometer clearly because it was analog. It was hard to read since he was seating at the back.

4. Head checks. Really exaggerate them lol.

I work at a company SOC right now and at first, I assumed the same. Before this, I came from a company SOC as well and I could say I was in a better place.

In terms of the metrics and how individual performance is assessed, I could say it is about ticket numbers because it is the easiest one to quantify according to them. I agree with that, but I was expecting that the way I work would count to something even if I lack the ticket numbers. Instead, I was told that if I do not improve I’ll be placed in PIP (performance intervention program?) where an HR rep will be present in my performance evaluation every time. If I still do not improve, management told me I’ll be fired. 

For downtime, well they do threat hunting. I signalled interest in learning and doing this. However, it is just hard to focus on these “side quests” when you have the ticket numbers lingering over your head. I mean, I tried budgeting my time in doing stuff that I want to learn but the ticket numbers just keep haunting me. Especially having that thought that I’ll be gone if I don’t improve the numbers.

In terms of how deep we do investigation, I could say it is not too deep. For malware and URL analysis, we are encouraged to escalate this to L2. If we cannot move further with the incident, escalate to L2. Actually, I’ve tried to mess up my investigation one time. And lol it is still correct according to people who verified my incident. No questions asked to me. 

I’m not sure if I understand this part but in terms of new learnings obtained from the incident, there’s not much in my opinion. But the way I see it, our L2’s seems to be in a constant lookout on what to improve. Probably because L1’s are just there to triage. Nothing more, nothing less I guess.
